title: SCUTOONS Live relay protocol v1
description: agents/research/LIVE.md B.6. One envelope per message, JSON over one WebSocket per client. The generator (deck/protocol/generate.ts) reads only the subset used here: object / string / integer / number / boolean / array / $ref / enum / const / oneOf discriminated by `kind` / additionalProperties maps. Edit this file, run `npm run generate -w shared/live`, commit both outputs.

Role.description: LIVE.md B.2. `uplink` is the local relay connected to the hosted one (B.6 Uplink). `reader` (#90, SHOW.md §7) is a phone reading the chapter: all it sends is its `story` events, to the conductor. `seat` (#90, SHOW.md §4) is a child conductor's relay in its parent's session, its group is the seat's id. `handheld` (#469, research/HANDHELD-CAMERA.md) is a phone as a handheld camera: it joins with the token the API hands it for one pairing code, all it sends is its `hand.*` messages, to the conductor (the storyboard editor), and it hears `hand.view`.

To.description: Who a message reaches. Every field narrows; all missing = everyone the sender may reach.

Envelope.description: B.6: `{ v: 1, seq, at?, from, to?, kind, p }`. `seq` is per session, assigned by the relay; `at` = relay time (ms) when the effect should happen.

seq.description: 0 before the relay stamped it (client → relay)

at.description: relay time in ms when the effect should happen

from.description: client id; `relay` for the relay's own messages

Message.description: `kind` + its payload `p`. One entry per B.6 message; a loose payload (`Loose`) marks a kind whose shape is not fixed yet.

oneOf.description: #236: a story event (`{ type, params, id? }`, the VNEvent) for the other decks – a trigger the receiving deck adapts itself (deck-events adapters/story.rs); the story keeps its own runner.

Loose.description: A payload whose shape B.6 names but this skeleton does not fix yet (say / line / fx / colour, cue actions).

VoteRule.description: B.11 (3): majority = most votes; groups = each group's majority is one vote; first = the first option to reach `n`.

VoteOpen.description: conductor → relay → the voting groups. `options` are the choice event's labels (index = option). The relay tallies, closes at `seconds` by itself and sends `vote.result`.

n.description: rule first: the votes an option needs

show.description: a voter sees the tally once they have voted (never before)

question.description: the choice event's question by locale (a phone shows its device's language, else the first); texts are locale maps

labels.description: `options` by locale, same order; `options` is the default

VoteClose.description: conductor → relay: close now; `override` = the conductor's option instead of the rule's.

VoteHold.description: conductor → relay: hold the vote – the countdown stops where it is, votes are still accepted; `hold: false` runs it on. The tally says `paused`.

VoteTally.description: relay → conductor every 250 ms while a vote is open (→ the audience too when the vote shows it).

left.description: ms until the vote closes by itself (stands still while held)

expected.description: the connected voting devices; the vote closes when all have voted

VoteResult.description: relay → everyone: the option the conductor applies as the choice event (B.1).

CellChange.description: conductor → relay → the outlet's clients on a row change: the outlet's new cell (B.5.2 `Cell`, resolved by the conductor – a deck renders it natively, #186).

Snapshot.description: What a client shows when it joins / reconnects / is moved (B.6): the last state, the current cell per outlet it sees, the open vote, the last instruction (say) per group it sees. The conductor sees every outlet and group.

media.description: the last `media.preload` per outlet it sees – a reconnecting output resolves its cell's media ids with it

decks.description: #188: every deck's being by client id (the conductor's snapshot)

sync.description: #195: the last `scene.sync`, if it is addressed to this client (a deck joining later syncs too; the conductor always sees it)

synced.description: #195: each deck's last `deck.synced` for that sync, by client id (the conductor's snapshot)

tempo.description: #321: the show clock's last anchor (every client but a bridge)

seat.description: #90: the parent's last word to this subtree (a conductor), or to this seat (a child relay)

seq.description: the session's seq when the snapshot was taken

Hello.description: client → relay, the first message. Audience / performer / musician / output join with the session code (+ group from their QR); conductor and bridge with a session token.

nick.description: trimmed to 24 characters by the relay

key.description: the `key` of this client's `welcome`: the proof that it is the client it names

Welcome.description: relay → client after `hello`: the snapshot of what this client should show now (B.6). On a `resume` inside the replay buffer the snapshot is empty and the missed messages follow.

key.description: this client's secret for a later `resume`; no other client ever sees it

Ping.description: client → relay. `t0`: the client's own clock when it sent the ping, in a unit of its choosing (the relay only echoes it; a deck sends µs – #321, the show clock's offset filter).

Pong.description: relay → the client: its `t0` back and the relay's time (ms) when the ping arrived – a sample of the relay's clock against the client's (deck-core `tempo::sync`).

Tempo.description: #321 (plan §3.7): the show clock's anchor – at relay ms `at` the show was at `beat`, running at `bpm` (or stopped: the beat stands), `per_bar` beats a bar. The leading deck (its picker, its scene's `lead`, or a deck on MIDI clock in – the venue's table-top clock) sends it only when its tempo line changed; the relay fills a missing `at` with now + the lead, keeps the last one for the snapshot and routes it to everyone else. The conductor may always lead; a deck leads while no other connected client does. Every deck on the show clock maps the anchor through its offset filter and follows the line.

at.description: relay ms; the envelope's `at` when missing

domain.description: #90: the clock domain, a sub conductor's own time; missing = "show", the top conductor's clock. A domain stays inside its subtree: each subtree is a session of its own and a parent's anchor only reaches the child's conductor, which takes it or keeps its own

State.description: conductor → relay on every change; folded into the snapshot.

Cue.description: conductor → relay; the relay splits `actions` per outlet → `to`. Actions are loose until the show schema (B.5) lands.

MediaPreload.description: conductor → relay → the outlet's clients before doors (LIVE.md B.5.6, #186): fetch and cache these, then answer `media.ready`. The relay keeps the last one per outlet for the snapshot.

SpotMode.description: #193: a set's spot carries rendered variants – a still, a rendered video, a 3D model; the Live view picks one.

MediaItem.description: One medium of a preload: `id` (what layers name as `media`) and either a `url` (show media under live/<toon>/ on the CDN, fetched with the deck token) or a set reference `set` + `spot` + `mode` (#193 – the deck resolves it: the API by id once the set model exists, today a local path / URL fallback).

set.description: a set id (#193: one staging of a place, e.g. `cathedral`)

spot.description: a named spot of the set (missing = the set's default view)

MediaReady.description: an outlet's client → relay → conductor: what of the outlet's preload is cached (`ready`) and what is not (`missing`, the reason per id in `why`) – the conductor's ready light. Sent after each preload and again while it retries.

CellMode.description: B.5.2: own = the cell's layers; mirror = what outlet `of` shows; black = black (a device outlet: all off).

Cell.description: B.5.2 `Cell` on the wire: what one outlet shows for the current row, resolved by the conductor (toon picks as toon + chapter + slice index, live media by preload id, sets by set + spot + mode). `layers` back → front.

of.description: mirror: the outlet whose cell this one shows

send.description: a device outlet: the messages on row enter

Layer.description: B.5.2 `Layer`: a source in a box of the outlet. `enter` / `exit` fade it in / out when the cell changes (missing = the outlet's default crossfade); a layer with the same id and source in both cells stays.

LayerBox.description: A box in % of the outlet (a panel's crop: of the slice); x, y = the top left corner. A layer without one fills the outlet.

Transition.description: A layer's fade when the cell changes, `ms` long (0 = a cut).

LayerSrc.description: What a layer shows (B.5.2 ToonSrc / LiveSrc, resolved). From the toon (the public library): scroll, slice, panel, surtitles. Live: video / image / model3d (a preloaded medium by id), set (a set's spot in a mode, #193), text, colour, camera. A show's cell: piece (#89).

PieceSrc.description: SHOW.md §5, a cell is a piece plus values: the piece (a place, `scene:nave`, `rig:storm`, `character:yellowmouse`) and all its values, resolved by the conductor along the path really taken (keep, values). The deck compares: same piece, the values glide; other piece, load and crossfade.

ToonChapter.description: scroll: the chapter's slices running one after the other.

ToonSlice.description: slice: one slice; `slice` = its index in the chapter's reading order (the slices with an image, 0-based – the conductor resolves the show's pick to it).

ToonPanel.description: panel: a crop of one slice (`crop` in % of the slice).

Surtitles.description: surtitles: the dialog of the slice the show is on (`state.slice`, an index like ToonSlice's) in `locale`; `of` = one character's lines only.

MediaSrc.description: a medium of the outlet's preload, by its id

SetSrc.description: #193: a set's spot in a mode – a use names set + spot, never a file. still / video = the spot's rendered variant as a picture; model3d = the set as the deck's 3D space, the camera at the spot.

TextSrc.description: text: a locale map (the deck shows its locale, else the first); `size` = the line height in % of the outlet height (default 6).

CameraSrc.description: camera: a video input on the output machine, by name (the deck's video-in – not built yet).

Kick.description: B.6: conductor → relay: the client is told (`error` code `kicked`) and its link ends; it joins again only with a new `hello`, which the conductor can answer the same way.

Rename.description: B.6: conductor → relay → that client. The relay cleans the nick (24 characters, the blocklist); empty = none.

Word.description: #90, SHOW.md §4b: how a child takes its parent's rows, a child treats its parent like a reader. follow = the row fires, suggest = its operator decides, free = ignored. The local GO always works.

Says.description: #90: what a parent's row says to its seat: `go` to a row of the child's, or `free`, it is left to itself; `none` only carries the word and the lock.

SeatWord.description: #90: conductor → its relay → the child relay in that seat (`to`: role seat, group the seat's id) → the child's conductor. The last one per seat is kept: a child conductor that joins later finds it in its snapshot.

lock.description: a lock from above: the parent's word wins over the child's own (SHOW.md §4b); only ever sent for a seat that may be locked

SeatState.description: #90: a child conductor's readout, up to its parent's relay, which keeps it per seat for the parent's presence.

clock.description: the clock domain it runs on; missing = the parent's

online.description: set by the parent's relay: false = the seat's link went away

Pinned.description: #90: a show at an exact version.

Flash.description: #90, SHOW.md §4b: one assignment, the tree resolved to exact versions. Goes down the tree seat by seat. A lock from above wins, otherwise the nearest wins, a deck may refuse; every deck reports what it runs.

shows.description: the root first, each show once

hops.description: how many conductors it came through; 0 = from this conductor's own operator

here.description: #91: the show of the conductor whose session it is in now, at the version the flash pins; a deck takes its outlet's cells of that one

id.description: #471: this flash's identity; a deck takes one flash once (a rejoin hands it the same one again)

by.description: #471: who flashed, for the deck's notice

skip.description: #471: the paths the operator left out, relative to the session it is in now (a client id; `<show>/…` for a sub conductor's session, the show its seat sits). A deck not named here takes it, also one that joins later

force.description: #471: the paths the prompt warned of and the operator accepted (asked not to be flashed, unsaved configuration): flashed anyway

FlashReport.description: #90: what a deck or conductor runs after a flash, to its conductor and on up. `from` of the envelope is the path it came along.

ready.description: #91: a deck has everything its outlet's cells name (the show and each piece); never blocks GO

lacks.description: #91: what it lacks, in words (deck-show's), one line each

keep.description: #471: the deck asks not to be flashed, and why (a request, not a lock)

unsaved.description: #471: the deck has configuration a flash would replace

mappings.description: #471: how many local mappings the deck has (they stay through a flash)

device.description: #471: native, browser, phone … (the flash list's filter)

kept.description: #471: the deck's own version, kept when a flash replaced it

own.description: #471: the deck runs its own kept version, not the flashed one

AddressFilter.description: #90, SHOW.md §9, for the workshop group and device. The receiver tests itself; a missing fact fails the filter.

Address.description: #90, SHOW.md §8: `kind:id > action`, down the tree. Whoever plays it picks up; finding nobody stays silent and is logged, it never goes up to a wider address.

id.description: the sender's, the answers carry it

AddressAnswer.description: #90: one receiver's count, up to the conductor that asked: it picked up (`reached`), passed the filter (`passed`), a handler took it (`answered`). A receiver the address does not name sends nothing.

Presence.description: relay → conductor: clients per group, who is ready; the decks that stream a being (#188 – a deck that left is gone from `decks`) and who sends values to whom (`routes`); each client's link (`links`, #223 – sent again when a client's rate changes); each deck's render quality (`quality`, #220 – sent again when a deck reports a change).

routes.description: every sender → receiver pair `deck.values` went along, sorted

links.description: #223: each client's link as the relay measures it, by client id (audience phones left out)

quality.description: #220: each deck's last `deck.quality`, by client id (a client that left is gone)

seats.description: #90: each seat's readout, by seat id

parent.description: #90: this relay's link to its parent; missing = it has none

LinkQuality.description: #223: one client's link: the smoothed WebSocket ping round trip, the rate the relay sends it state-like messages at (`deck.values`, `presence`, `vote.tally`, `state` – 30 = as fast as they come, down to 5 on a link that can't carry more), and how many of them it replaced before they went out (a stalled client gets the newest, not a backlog).

rtt.description: ms; missing before the first pong

Route.description: #188: a deck's values flow from client `from` to client `to` (the conductor's scene draws a hose between their beings).

DeckGraph.description: #188 phase 4: a deck → relay → the conductor, on joining and when its scene changes: its being – the stage graph's nodes and links (the body), the head's character, the body's size (m), the moods calm → wild, the exposed parameters. The relay keeps the last one per client for the conductor's snapshot.

DeckValues.description: #188 phase 4 (the stream #189's sends build on): a deck → relay → the conductor (and `to`, if set), only what changed, at most 30 / s (the relay drops the rest). `values`: a path – `node.port` (a control input, a control output, an audio output's block peak) or `node.shape` (an LFO's waveform) – → a float vector (1 … n components; one today). `mood`: the head's mood when it changed. Not kept for replay: the relay folds them into the snapshot's `decks`.

DeckMidi.description: #211: a deck → relay → the conductor (and `to`, if set): MIDI its parameters send as outputs (a mapping's target `port = "conductor"` – CC / note / pitch bend, status byte first), for the conductor to route on like device input. Only decks send it; not kept for replay (a value stream, not state).

HandPose.description: #469: a handheld → relay → the conductor: the phone's own pose in its world (the editor maps it onto the shot camera). `t` = the phone's clock (ms), `p` = position (metres, 3 numbers), `q` = rotation (quaternion x y z w, 4 numbers). Latest wins: on QUIC a datagram; a pose not newer than the last one from that phone is dropped (by the relay and by the receiving client); never logged or replayed.

HandMode.description: #469: what the phone tracks – WebXR (position + rotation), the orientation sensor (rotation only), nothing yet.

HandState.description: #469: a handheld → the conductor: what it tracks and whether tracking holds; `ua` its browser. Reliable; sent again after every welcome.

ua.description: at most 300 characters (the client trims it)

HandRecord.description: #469: a handheld → the conductor: Record (`on`) or Stop. Reliable (`hand.recenter`: Recenter, no payload).

HandView.description: #469: the conductor (the storyboard editor) → its handhelds: the shot it films, whether the handheld camera is on for it, recording and for how long (s). Reliable; sent again after every welcome.

DeckListen.description: #442: a deck → relay → the group `decks`: the absolute addresses its far world nodes name (deck-space rig/address.rs: `/deck:<name>/scene:<id>/character:<id>/<track>:<node>.<port>`), sent on each welcome and again every 10 s while it has any (a subscription not refreshed for 30 s lapses). The deck whose name and rig the address names answers with `deck.events` to this client; the relay never parses an address. Ordered, not kept for replay.

DeckEvents.description: #442: a deck → relay → one subscriber (`to.client`): what left the event outputs it asked for, in order, as deck-events events by name – the world node's `listen` filters them on arrival. Ordered, never merged or replayed (a value stream, not state).

address.description: the absolute address the subscriber asked for

dur_s.description: a note's length in seconds (beats become seconds on the sender's tempo map); missing = a moment

SceneSync.description: #195: conductor → relay → the decks (the group `decks`, or only the client ids in `decks`): fetch what this scene needs into the cache – the same scene-content request (`GET /api/library/scene-content`) and cache as a deck's own scene, skipping what is there – and answer `deck.synced`. Only the conductor sends it; the relay logs it and keeps the last one for the snapshot, so a deck that joins later syncs too.

scene.description: the scene / show id the sync is for (`deck.synced` names it back)

sets.description: set ids – each deck fetches the set's 3D at its own quality

characters.description: character ids – every portrait the API lists

beings.description: #191: lent beings – reserved, no deck reads it yet

decks.description: only these client ids (missing = every deck)

SyncState.description: #195: syncing = files still to settle; ready = every item is in the cache; missing = settled, but some item is not there (`why`); offline = the API can't be reached and some item is not in the cache.

QualityLevel.description: #220: a deck's render quality level, cheapest first – the hardware tiers S / M / L / XL (deck/HARDWARE.md).

DeckQuality.description: #220: a deck → relay, when its quality changes (at once) and its frame time moved (at most every 2 s): the level it renders at now, the render scale (× the screen; > 1 supersamples), whether the governor steps it (`auto`) and the mean frame interval (ms). The relay keeps the last one per client and hands it to the conductor in presence (`quality`), next to the link.

frame.description: ms, the mean of the last half second

ceiling.description: the level chosen (the governor steps at most up to it); missing = `level`

DeckSynced.description: #195: a deck → relay → the conductor, while it works on a `scene.sync` (progress) and when it is done – like `media.ready`. Items are `set:<id>` and `character:<id>`; one in neither list is still syncing. The relay keeps each deck's last one for the conductor's snapshot (`synced`) and marks a deck ready in presence once its state is ready.

DeckState.description: A deck's being in the conductor's snapshot: its graph and its latest values (all of them, folded).

DeviceMsg.description: One message for a device, resolved against the venue patch. `midi`: raw bytes (status + data). `osc`: address + typed args. `dmx`: channel values of the outlet's universe (a look resolves to one per fixture).

OscArg.description: One OSC argument, typed (JSON alone cannot tell 2 from 2.0). On the wire: int32, float32, string, bool. Blobs / timetags come when something needs them.

OscMessage.description: An OSC message (in or out): the address pattern and its arguments. Bundles are flattened by the adapter.

DmxMessage.description: DMX out (#187): `values` from channel `ch` on (1-based; ch + values − 1 ≤ 512) in the outlet's universe; `fade` ms from the current values (missing / 0 = at once). Several ranges = several messages in `msgs`.

DeviceIn.description: bridge → conductor: MIDI / OSC in, mapped to actions there.

Devices.description: bridge → relay: the ports the bridge sees, for the patch UI.

Error.description: relay → client (not in B.6; the relay's refusals: bad hello, unknown kind, rate limit).
